# E4 Variant One Experimentation Log

## Definition and Goals

The following corresponds to a end to end test of the reliability and fault tolerance of the ML API and subsequently de CSA under a failure to receive valid replies from Classification Reuqests towards the ML API. In order to test this , the entire topology will be raised and subsequently the ML API controller will be directly shut down such that all classification attempts fail with a timeout failure.

These events should be recorded by the CSA in its log who will have access to the entire topolgoy and controller side configuration.As such, the experiment will only remove from the deplopyed  topoology the ML API and will simulate a failure on that node only. The CSA will then receive a singular PacketIn notification from an ICMP echo request between hosts Golf and Hotel, in the direction from left to right,to attempt to start the classification process.

Since the CSA can reach readiness if the topological information required is present, the state of the network will allow it to reach the `control-plane-readiness=True` state whicih shall be recorded in the lgos after approximately 60-70 readiness attempts until the CSA configures itself properly. Once this happens, the application will stop emitting logs and we shall attempt to initialize a classification process with the API down.

### Goals

1. Showcase the ability of the CSA to reach readiness through topology and TE knowledge only, while retaining operational capacity even in the face of classification failures that make classifying incoming traffic impossible.
2. Showcase the ability of the CSA, and its separation of responsibilities, to allow for it to resume its normal processing abilities once the ML API has been restarted through an ICMP echo request classification process


## Steps to be done

1. Start the entire toplogy and use PostMAN RESTCONF requests to configure the controller and its related state to the topology,
2. Await for confirmation on Control plane readiness from the CSA in its logs, record the returned message in here
3. Shut down the ML API directly through the VSCodeContainerlab topology view mode
4. Start an initial classification processing round for a single ICMP echo request between golf -> hotel and store the state that the CSA reaches
5. Restart the ML API
6. Start a second classiication round for the same count of ICMP echo requests pacakets and evaluate the final topological state, it should resultin a complete update of the CSA logs,registries, and router state

As can be seen in the logs,the result of a packet received notification follos the orpoer channels of packet feature extraction and the attemptedclassification of the packet. At the classification stage, since the classiifer cache was empt y, the cappliciationa ttmepted to perform a classification call through the ClassificationService oriented towards interconnecting the application towards the ML API whose processing failed (in this case timed out) and cuase the exception to be raised and the processing to fail . It is impnt to note that this did not result in an error in the application that cause it to crash ,rather the application raemained functionall ,although tdegraded,as it cannot fulfill its main  . The subseuqent update to th e freshness of the topology indicates all of its subsystems aere working, it is just the classification serivce that fails . As reported by the CSA metrics exposed through its YANG  model the entirey system is still ready and its refehses are valid as wlel as the information recorede within th e router,switche and lsp record
